claim: Held visual contents bias attention toward matching items under suitable conditions: with one held item and a short gap, an invalid (matching) distractor slows search by about 55-85 ms against neutral (Soto and Humphreys 2008: 1,209 vs 1,146; 1,049 vs 991; 1,101 vs 1,015 ms).
agent_test: Hold a lesson in context, then give a task where a distractor matches the lesson wording; compare errors with a neutral lesson at equal tokens.

claim: Memory-driven capture is not automatic in all conditions: Woodman and Luck (2007) found no cost with one item and a long delay (1,475 vs 1,505 ms; 1,455 vs 1,458 ms, N=10 each), and later work concludes that maintenance alone is not sufficient for guidance.
agent_test: Compare a held lesson that is the active task goal with one that is only stored; test whether the stored one biases output.

claim: The load pattern is contested: Woodman and Luck found a 67 ms benefit (not cost) with three held items and a matching distractor; Soto and Humphreys found costs with 1-2 items; Hollingworth and Beck found capture at load 1 but not reliably at load 2 with one match, restored when two items match. Load theory and biased competition each fit part of this.
agent_test: Vary the number of held lessons (1, 2, 4, 8) with one matching distractor; measure distractor-following rate at equal tokens.

claim: Two-item capture has been replicated by several labs (Chen and Du 2017; Fan 2019, 2021; King and Macnamara 2020; Zhang 2018; Zhou 2020). A large-sample replication (56 analysed) found capture at load 1 but Bayes factors of 0.12-0.16 for no difference at load 2 with a single match.
agent_test: Test whether the number of matching held items, not the number held, predicts bias in the agent.

claim: Capture scales with the number of matching held items: Match-2 124 ms vs Match-1 68 ms (Hollingworth and Beck 2016, N=24).
agent_test: Present 1 vs 2 held lessons both matching the same distractor; compare error rates.

claim: Matching distractors draw the first eye movement in natural scenes: fixated on 23.6% of trials vs 11.0% when mismatching (about double).
agent_test: No direct test; analogue is first-step choice following a held cue.

claim: Capture needs an active template: deprioritised held items do not capture (Hollingworth and Hwang 2013; Olivers et al. 2011), and when the same target repeats, the template leaves working memory (CDA -0.8 uV falling to -0.30 uV; no CDA with a constant target).
agent_test: Compare a lesson restated every step with one shown once and repeated; check whether bias shrinks as it becomes routine.

claim: Repeated memorising of the same item lowers memory-driven bias within one or two trials, while memory improves.
agent_test: Repeat a lesson across turns; measure bias to matching distractors by turn.

claim: Memory-driven capture depends on time and mental effort: lag-2 accuracy 75.2% vs lag-7 81.9% (d=0.42, N=58), and the waxing and waning disappears with arithmetic between (80.0 vs 80.1%). Longer ISI also raised the match effect (about 150 to 250 ms).
agent_test: Insert a delay or unrelated work between lesson and test; measure decay of the bias.

claim: Distractors that match held contents are actively suppressed after capture (Pd at 250-300 ms, N=12, onset about 220 ms vs about 120 ms for singletons), suggesting a late rejection stage.
agent_test: Add an explicit distractor-rejection check after retrieval and measure whether matching distractors are filtered.

claim: Negative templates (held cue says what to ignore) mostly fail to speed search: Becker 2015 found no advantage in three experiments, plus Berggren and Eimer 2021, Williams 2020, Cunningham and Egeth 2016 and four unpublished nulls; only a small informal demonstration shows benefit. LLM side: negated questions drive larger models below random (NeQA, 1,428 items), so naming the forbidden item likely primes it (d12).
agent_test: Compare 'do not use X' lessons with positive lessons at equal tokens.

claim: LLMs are distracted by irrelevant context: of base problems solved at baseline, no more than 18% stay solved across all distractor types; code-davinci-002 COT micro 72.4%, macro 6.0%; text-davinci-003 macro 0 on role-overlap distractors with more than 2 steps (Shi et al. 2023; checked against the paper table by the cross-checker).
agent_test: Add a topically related but irrelevant lesson to a task; measure macro accuracy across distractor types at equal tokens.

claim: Mitigations help only partly: an ignore instruction lifts COT micro 72.4 to 77.8 and macro 6.0 to 15.0; self-consistency adds about 11 micro points (35.5 for 0-shot COT); LTM+SC reaches micro 93.4, macro 45.0. Exemplars containing distractors help; complicated prompts hurt multi-step problems. A later adaptive attack found prompt mitigations within +/-0.03.
agent_test: Test ignore-instruction vs self-consistency vs exemplar-with-distractor at equal tokens.

claim: Related distractors hurt more than random ones in LLMs, matching feature-match capture: Wu et al. 2024 (related irrelevant info misleads more; more items distract more) and Yoran et al. 2024 (wrong answer entity in context in 77% of errors with low-ranked context vs 37% with random). Kukreja 2026 adds scale effects (related exponent -0.135 shrinks; random +0.217 grows).
agent_test: Vary similarity of the distractor lesson to the target (same entity, same topic, random); compare error rate.

claim: Contextual entrainment: Llama-3.1-8B raises the logit of any token already in context, even random (+4.01) or irrelevant (+4.92) vs related (+4.08); a small set of heads (3.2-10.7%; 36 heads = 3.5% for country-capital) mediates it; ablating them widens the counterfactual logit gap 7.69 to 13.20 (checked against the paper). Replicated by two 2026 papers: shared heads (2-4%) in Liu and Chu, and a shared global head core in Zheng and Shi (recovery 1.464).
agent_test: Mechanistic, open models only; behavioural analogue is echo of in-context tokens in agent output.

claim: Distractor entrainment scales in opposite directions: larger models resist counterfactual context more (b=-0.330) but copy arbitrary tokens more (+0.217); the largest are about 4x more resistant to counterfactual and about 2x more prone to arbitrary copying (Cerebras-GPT, Pythia). Liu and Chu 2026 (26 LLMs) confirm entrainment falls with size (Qwen3 3.91 at 0.6B to 3.35 at 32B) while counterfactual entrainment rises slightly.
agent_test: Check at two model sizes whether a pure-noise lesson is echoed.

claim: Adaptive adversarial distractors reveal the weakness that static ones do not: over seven models accuracy 0.843 to 0.323 (52.0% drop); Claude-3.5-Sonnet 0.879 to 0.495; static GSM-IC distractors only 1.8% average drop on advanced models (checked against the paper).
agent_test: Run a search-based adversarial lesson attack on the agent; compare with static distractors.

claim: Position and length matter beyond content: accuracy falls below closed-book when the answer is in the middle (GPT-3.5 56.1% closed-book, oracle 88.3%; Claude-1.3 48.3%, oracle 76.1%; checked against the paper); accuracy falls 0.92 to 0.68 at 3,000 tokens; premise order can cost over 30%; serial position effects are widespread.
agent_test: Place the held lesson at start, middle and end of context at equal tokens; measure effect on target use.

claim: Held context can hurt even when the model knows better: anchoring in 22% to 61% of questions (Qwen2.5-0.5B 60.5% to Qwen3-235B thinking 22.0%); user-suggested wrong answers cut accuracy by up to 27%; biasing prompts cut accuracy by up to 36%; a knowledge-enhancement prompt made anchoring worse (34.7 to 50.5%).
agent_test: Seed a wrong anchor lesson; test whether a counter-instruction or a fresh-context re-solve removes it.

claim: Errors compound through memory: snowballed hallucinations in 95% of failed cases; intrinsic self-correction often turns correct to incorrect (GPT-3.5 keeps first answer 74.7% on GSM8K); evaluator bias propagates through agent memory (length bias A=13.18) but not always (authority bias A=0.00).
agent_test: Inject one bad lesson in memory; measure spread to later tasks and test a gated memory write.

claim: Agent memory retrieval is similarity driven, so a past record that resembles the query tends to be copied; history-based deletion with a strict evaluator helped.
agent_test: Compare retrieval of top-k similar lessons vs dissimilar-but-relevant ones at equal tokens.

claim: Working-memory-like limits in LLMs are unclear: ChatGPT shows a human-like drop at n=3; best models 90.08%, 90.08%, 84.75% at n=8-10; an ICE benchmark found two small models scoring 0% even in clean controls (a floor effect, not evidence of load).
agent_test: Use only as a capacity baseline, not as a load-theory test.

claim: Machine models of biased competition exist (normalisation model, Deco and Rolls, ATTNet) but none were numerically read, and no direct test of load theory vs biased competition in an LLM was found.
agent_test: Design a new test: held lesson matches a distractor under high vs low task load, at equal tokens.

claim: The human evidence base is small: most key studies have N=10-24 per experiment and some load contrasts rest on non-significant differences (Exp 4 p=.077), so effect sizes are uncertain.
agent_test: Run agent tests with 30+ seeds and report Bayes factors, not single p values.

claim: Founding neural result (abstracts only): in monkey IT, held cue activity persists in the delay, and 2-5 choice items compete; non-target responses are suppressed 90-120 ms before the saccade (Chelazzi 1993) and the non-target influence is eliminated within 150-200 ms of array onset (Chelazzi 1998). Downing (2000) shows attention shifts to the item matching a held sample, with the opposite pattern when no memory is required.
agent_test: Hold a lesson vs show the same lesson without holding it; compare which item the agent attends to.

claim: Capture is not removed by a task-switch cue or interruption (Hautekiet, Lewis-Peacock, Olivers 2026, two pre-registered experiments) and is stronger in feature search than singleton mode (Won and Zhang 2025).
agent_test: Add a 'now do the task' reminder after a lesson and check whether the pull on a matching distractor persists.

claim: In humans capture costs time more than errors: matching distractors slowed search but added no accuracy cost (Kim et al. 2026), and the extra cost arises after the distractor is fixated, where higher WMC reduces dwell (Liu, Wang, Liu 2026). Based on abstracts only.
agent_test: Log steps or tokens as well as error rate in the lesson-match test.

claim: Contextual entrainment holds at sentence level across 26 LLMs: Llama-3.1-8B accuracy 79.4% to 22.4% with a counterfactual sentence; 6-model average 74.1 to 55.9 (factual) and 46.5 (counterfactual); the model's own earlier answer as context costs 4.3 points. Instruction tuning cuts loss 40-70% but never to zero.
agent_test: Plant a true but off-topic sentence in the lesson style and measure answer copying; also test the agent's own prior notes.

claim: LLM-side gaps not closed by any found study: (1) held-lesson match crossed with task load, (2) match count vs number held, (4) restate-every-step vs once, (8) position x similarity, (10) lag decay. Search was partial (APIs rate-limited).
agent_test: Our own factorial test at equal tokens.
